explain.say: Saleem Sinai tells us he was born in Bombay at the exact stroke of midnight on the fifteenth of August 1947, the very moment India became independent. He is the narrator of Salman Rushdie's 1981 novel, and his life is chained to his country's history. The timeline follows both together.

explain.say: Look at the map. Saleem is born in Bombay, now Mumbai, moves to Karachi in Pakistan, is caught up in the 1971 war that created Bangladesh, then lives in Delhi before returning to Bombay. Partition, the 1947 split of British India into India and Pakistan, runs through his family. Why might Rushdie send one boy across all these borders?

draw.label: Saleem’s journey: Bombay, Karachi, the 1971 war in what became Bangladesh, Delhi, and Bombay again

explain.say: Now the magic. All 1,001 children born in that first midnight hour have powers. Saleem can hear thoughts and gathers the children in his head like a parliament. This is magic realism, where the impossible is told as calmly as the everyday. Rushdie uses it to picture a newborn nation's hopes. What power would you give a new country?

explain.say: Look at the swap. A nurse switches two babies, so poor-born Saleem grows up rich and rich-born Shiva grows up poor. Saleem's gifts are a huge nose and telepathy, joining voices; Shiva's are powerful knees, force and war. In the Emergency of 1975 to 1977, Shiva helps the government crush the children. What might the two boys stand for?

Saleem tells all this to his listener Padma while working in a pickle factory, and each chapter is like a jar of pickled memory, preserved but changed. He admits he gets some dates wrong, so he is an unreliable narrator. The novel won the Booker Prize in 1981. Brilliant. Challenge: tell one historical date through your own family's story.

faq.a: A style in which magical or impossible events are narrated in a matter-of-fact way inside a realistic world. Gabriel García Márquez and Rushdie are famous examples; it often expresses histories that plain realism cannot hold.

faq.q: Why is Saleem born at midnight important?
faq.a: Born at the exact moment of independence, he is handcuffed to history: his life mirrors the nation's, from hopeful birth through wars and the Emergency, so his body and family become a metaphor for India.

The 1,001 children born in India's first hour of independence, each with a magical gift; the nearer to midnight, the greater the power. Saleem links them by telepathy in the Midnight Children's Conference.

faq.q: Who is Shiva in Midnight's Children?
faq.a: The child born at the same instant as Saleem and swapped with him at birth. Gifted with deadly knees, he becomes a war hero and later helps hunt down the midnight's children during the Emergency.

From 1975 to 1977 Prime Minister Indira Gandhi suspended elections and civil liberties, jailed opponents and ran forced sterilisation drives. In the novel, the Widow's government destroys the children's powers.

facts: Midnight's Children won the Booker Prize in 1981.
It was named the Booker of Bookers in 1993 and the Best of the Booker in 2008.
In the novel, 1,001 children are born in the first hour of India's independence.
